methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: ODU and Google launch AI incubator to boost innovation in Hampton Roads - MSN
signals.signal_reading: ODU-Google AI incubator represents institutional capacity-building in a traditionally non-tech hub, potentially distributing deep AI fluency through structured peer learning beyond NoVA's gravity well.

signals.title: Healthcare providers say AI helps them focus on patients. But it also raises questions about privacy, security and the role of humans in medicine
signals.signal_reading: Healthcare AI adoption in underserved regions shows platform-delivered tools enabling broad but shallow use—doctors consume AI for note-taking without building underlying capability, epitomizing distributed convenience over depth.

signals.title: Pentagon Expands Scale AI Deal to $500M and AI Defense Firm TurbineOne Moves HQ to Northern Virginia - Clearance Jobs
signals.signal_reading: Pentagon's $500M Scale AI expansion and TurbineOne HQ relocation to NoVA intensifies defense-AI concentration where federal procurement dollars deepen expertise in metro corridors while bypassing rural workforce development.

signals.title: EPA grant backs community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: EPA-funded community-driven workforce training at Virginia Tech signals potential for distributed skill-building in coal-transition regions, testing whether grassroots capacity development can counter metro concentration dynamics.

signals.title: Problem-solvers by nature: How Virginia Beach Fire put AI to work - FireRescue1
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Beach Fire's problem-solving approach to AI implementation demonstrates municipal-level technical agency outside tech hubs, suggesting distributed depth emerges when regional institutions own adaptation rather than consume platforms.
